newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta sees no spring trucking bans this week.
newsitem.headline: Alberta sees no spring trucking bans this week.

text.p: Bans on grain trucking on Alberta's rural roads tentatively set for Thursday will not come into effect until probably next week, a provincial highway department spokeswoman told Reuters on Wednesday.
"It won't be this week, the weather here is too bad," an Alberta Transportation spokeswoman said.
Weight restrictions on Prairie highways are an annual occurence because winter freeze pressures water up from the water shelf into the road bed where it freezes and expands.
The spring thaw melts the ice and displaces the highway's foundation making it vulnerable to damage from heavy trucks.
Limited loads are permitted during the spring thaw.
Alberta had planned to institute bans on March 13, followed by Saskathchewan on March 16 and Manitoba March 23.
Road bans mean a smaller amount of grain can be trucked to primary elevators than at any other time of the crop year.
Last spring Alberta introduced the Prairie's first road bans on March 14, followed by Saskatchewan on March 17 and Manitoba on March 25.
